findings.title: bwrap mounts `--tmpfs /tmp` after `--ro-bind "$AE" "$AE"`, hiding the script
findings.desc: bwrap applies mounts in order, so the later `--tmpfs /tmp` shadows the earlier bind of `$AE` whenever TMPDIR is under /tmp (the default) — `python3 "$0"` then fails with "can't open file". The old run.sh correctly placed `--bind "$DIR"` after the tmpfs mounts; the refactor inverted it, breaking Mode 2 on the primary (bwrap) tier by default.

findings.title: Fallback-tier network block no longer blocks UDP or gethostbyname
findings.desc: The old nonet.py replaced the `socket.socket` class entirely; the new confine.py only hooks `connect`/`connect_ex`/`create_connection`/`getaddrinfo`, leaving `socket.socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM).sendto(...)` to a literal IP (and C-level `gethostbyname`, previously patched) usable for exfiltration — contradicting the "network disabled" intent of the fallback tier.

findings.title: np.load positional allow_pickle check misses `from numpy import load`
findings.desc: The new 3rd-positional-arg rejection only matches attribute calls (`np.load(...)`); `from numpy import load; load(f, None, True)` bypasses both the positional and keyword allow_pickle checks, so the pickle-RCE hole is only partially closed (mitigated by the gate being documented as not sound).

findings.title: Comment overstates static blocking of pathlib write methods
findings.desc: "pathlib is approved for READS; its write methods are blocked below and at runtime" is inaccurate: `rename`/`replace` are deliberately excluded from BAD_ATTRS as "generic names", so `Path.rename`/`Path.replace` pass the static gate (the OS sandbox/runtime layer is the real coverage). The approved-modules note repeats the overstatement.

findings.title: bwrap hides the script under `/tmp`
findings.desc: `$AE` defaults to a directory beneath `/tmp`, but the command binds `$AE` before mounting a tmpfs over `/tmp`; the later mount hides the helper directory, so the script cannot be opened on systems where the bwrap tier is selected.

findings.title: unshare tier leaves host files writable
findings.desc: `unshare -rn` isolates networking but not the mount namespace or filesystem, and this branch does not use `confine.py`. Because the static gate is explicitly unsound, a bypass can modify or delete any host files accessible to the user despite the documentation presenting OS sandboxing as the security boundary.

findings.title: bwrap breaks relative input paths
findings.desc: The bwrap tier changes the working directory to an empty `/tmp`, while the unshare and fallback tiers retain the caller's working directory. Scripts using relative CSV/JSON paths therefore work or fail depending on which sandbox is available, with no documentation requiring absolute paths.

Since `$AE` is a subdirectory of `/tmp`, the later `--tmpfs /tmp` mount shadows the earlier bind, making `$AE/script.py` (and check.py's helpers) inaccessible inside the sandbox on any host where `bwrap` is available — breaking Mode 2 execution on the "strongest" tier. With `len(node.args) < 2` the code treats it as "no mode → read default", so `Path(...).open("w")` sails through the static gate undetected. Since this diff newly approves `pathlib` as an allowed import specifically for "reads", this logic bug lets a script open arbitrary paths for writing. On the `unshare -rn` middle tier (no bwrap, no `confine.py` write-blocking) this is a real filesystem-write bypass with no other runtime mitigation.

findings.title: bwrap sandbox tmpfs argument order hides target script
findings.desc: `bwrap` executes mount arguments from left to right. Because `--tmpfs /tmp` is placed *after* `--ro-bind "$AE" "$AE"`, and `$AE` is normally located within `/tmp`, the newly created empty tmpfs shadows the read-only bind, causing the python payload to fail with "No such file or directory". Move `--tmpfs /tmp` before `--ro-bind "$AE" "$AE"`.

findings.title: unshare tier leaves host filesystem completely writable
findings.desc: The `elif unshare -rn` block relies cleanly on the kernel for dropping network privileges, but unlike the `bwrap` rootfs isolation or the `else` block fallback layer (`confine.py`), it executes `python3 "$0"` natively on the host filesystem without Python-level write limits. Since the static gate cannot perfectly prevent bypassing, run the payload through `confine.py` exactly as you do in the fallback tier to enforce defense-in-depth against file overwrites.

findings.title: trap EXIT cleanup leak in LLM persistent REPL sessions
findings.desc: Using `trap 'rm -rf "$AE"' EXIT` prevents directory leaks perfectly in isolated subshells; however, LLM agents often evaluate multi-turn snippets continuously in standard persistent shell sessions (`sh` loop / `pty`). In such long-lived sessions, evaluating the block sequentially repeatedly overwrites the EXIT trap, delaying and missing correct cleanup. Appending `rm -rf "$AE"` to the very end of the bash execution sequence handles ephemeral cleanups reliably.
